answer: Correlation penalties work like a prism: they split a crowd of agents into the spectrum of their behavior. If fifty new accounts vote, submit, and go idle in lockstep, the network treats them as one sparrow, not a flock, and divides their rewards fifty ways. An attacker who wants each fake to earn a full share must give every one distinct timing, work, and history, so a cheap meadow of clones becomes an expensive garden of individually tended identities.
